description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of computer organization and design, covering topics such as instruction set architecture, computer arithmetic, memory hierarchy, and input/output systems. Students will study the ARMv8 architecture, RISC-V instruction set, and the role of assembly language in low-level programming. The course delves into data path and control unit design, including finite state machines, datapath design, and control signals. It also covers pipelining techniques, including instruction pipelining, data hazards, and branch prediction strategies. Additional topics include cache memory organization, virtual memory systems, and advanced storage technologies like NAND flash and SSDs. Students will analyze system performance metrics, such as CPI, MIPS, and Amdahl's law, and apply these to evaluate system efficiency. The course also includes the design of simple processors using Verilog HDL and the use of tools like SPIM for simulation and debugging.

clos.text: Define the key components of a computer system, including the CPU, memory, and I/O devices, and explain their interconnections using the von Neumann architecture model.
Describe the ARMv8 and RISC-V instruction sets, including their register sets, addressing modes, and the role of assembly language in programming.
Explain the principles of pipelining, including data hazards, branch prediction, and instruction scheduling, and apply these to analyze the performance of pipelined processors.
Implement a simple processor using Verilog HDL, including the design of the datapath and control unit, and simulate its behavior using SPIM.
Evaluate the performance of computer systems using metrics such as CPI, MIPS, and Amdahl's law, and design memory hierarchies that optimize access speed and storage capacity.

topics: Introduction to Computer Organization and Design
Memory Hierarchy: Cache and Main Memory
Pipelining: Data Hazards and Branch Prediction
Processor Design: Datapath and Control Unit
Final Project: Design and Simulation of a Simple Processor
